heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Bambu PAHT-CF exceptionally well out of the box thanks to its factory hardened steel nozzle and heated chamber enclosure. With a maximum volumetric flow rate of 11 mm³/s, the safe operational print speed tops out at 131 mm/s for a standard 0.4mm nozzle profile.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate or High-Temp Plate with Bambu Liquid Glue / PVP Glue Stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 11 mm³/s under Filament Settings to prevent extruder skipping and under-extrusion at speeds above 131 mm/s.
Disable the Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan completely (0%) to eliminate severe thermal shock and warping across high-temperature polyamide layers.
Configure Part Cooling Fan threshold to min 0% and max 20%, keeping it off for the first 3 layers to guarantee high layer bonding strength.
Set Line Width to 0.45mm on perimeters and enable an inner brim (5mm) with zero brim-object gap to mechanically stabilize sharp corners.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing, surface pockmarks, and extrusion popping sounds
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excess moisture absorbed into the hygroscopic high-temperature nylon matrix vaporizing violently inside the 285°C hotend.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated blast oven or print chamber at 80°C for 8 to 12 hours before printing, and feed directly from an active dry box or desiccated AMS.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and print warping from build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Inadequate bed adhesion and excessive chamber heat loss or differential thermal contraction between nylon and the plate.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Raise bed temperature to 100°C, apply a uniform layer of liquid glue/glue stick release agent, keep the door and top glass shut, and allow chamber temperature to soak to 45°C+ before printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Premature nozzle clogging during mid-print retractions
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Heat creep exacerbated by prolonged exposure to high chamber temperatures, or carbon fiber aggregation in standard 0.4mm clearance.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase print temperature to 290°C to lower melt viscosity, avoid opening the top glass, verify cold-block fan functionality, and perform cold pulls with nylon cleaning filament.

faq.question: Can I feed Bambu PAHT-CF through the standard Bambu AMS unit?
faq.answer: Yes, Bambu PAHT-CF is formulated to be sufficiently flexible and less brittle on spools than standard PA-CF, making it fully compatible with the AMS provided the desiccant is completely fresh.

faq.question: Why is the print speed capped at 131 mm/s on the X1C?
faq.answer: The high viscosity and carbon fiber filler of PAHT-CF safely allow a maximum volumetric flow rate of 11 mm³/s; at a standard 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm extrusion width, 131 mm/s reaches that volumetric ceiling.

faq.question: Do I need to leave the X1C door or top glass open when printing PAHT-CF?
faq.answer: No, absolutely keep the door and top glass fully closed. Polyamide requires a warm, draft-free chamber environment (45°C-50°C) to prevent thermal stress, delamination, and warping.

faq.question: Is a glue stick mandatory on the Textured PEI plate for PAHT-CF?
faq.answer: Yes, glue stick acts primarily as a release agent to prevent high-adhesion high-temperature nylon from tearing the PEI coating off the steel sheet upon cooling.
